blocks.text: You asked where Ridgeline should focus to win its first federal work. Ridgeline does janitorial, HVAC maintenance and grounds work for commercial clients in Georgia and has no federal awards on record yet.

**The short version:** the biggest janitorial contracts in Georgia are not open to Ridgeline, because the law reserves many of them for AbilityOne nonprofits. Go after the smaller, competed, small-business work instead: USDA Forest Service janitorial and recreation-area work in Georgia and South Carolina, the Defense Department schools custodial contract at Fort Stewart, and HVAC and grounds subcontracts under the large Georgia facility contracts. Bid the open Forest Service job due December 17 first.

sections.heading: Pathways in priority order: where to focus

rows.path: USDA Forest Service, Georgia and South Carolina ranger districts
rows.why: Small janitorial and recreation-site jobs set aside for small business, the right size for a first prime award, and they combine cleaning with grounds and trash, which is Ridgeline's mix
rows.evidence: Open: Francis Marion Ranger District office janitorial, small business set-aside, due Dec 17, 2026. Planned: Chattooga River recreation janitorial and garbage, $500K to $999K, FY2027, base plus 4 option years

rows.path: Defense Department schools (DoDEA), Fort Stewart custodial
rows.why: Competed under a small business set-aside and sized for a firm Ridgeline's size; it is a real target, unlike the AbilityOne contracts
rows.evidence: HE125425CE002, Residential Enhancements, $1.2M obligated of a $3.1M ceiling; current period ends Jan 31, 2027 with options to Jul 31, 2030

rows.path: Subcontracts under large Georgia facility contracts
rows.why: Builds the federal past performance Ridgeline lacks, using its HVAC and grounds crews, while it bids its own small jobs
rows.evidence: FLETC dorm management at Glynco, T47 International, $54.9M, runs to Sep 30, 2027. Commercial small primes already winning Georgia custodial work: Unique Cleaning Service (78 awards, 6 agencies), Nobis Enterprises, EBS-4U

blocks.text: Fort Stewart is second, not first, because its options run to 2030: the work comes back early only if the school agency does not exercise the January 2027 option. Introduce Ridgeline now so it is on the list either way.

sections.heading: Buyer pain points: what these buyers are under pressure to fix

blocks.text: In Georgia, the Army, the Federal Law Enforcement Training Center, the Air Force and the CDC buy the most janitorial services (about $123M, $95M, $30M and $29M over FY2023 to FY2025). Most of that money sits in a few very large contracts.

Policy shapes this market: under FAR Subpart 8.7, agencies must buy services on the AbilityOne Procurement List from AbilityOne nonprofits, with no other exception, and custodial work is one of the largest listed categories. Contracts not on the list are competed normally.

For Ridgeline this means the volume is with large primes and AbilityOne nonprofits. The open doors are the smaller civilian sites (Forest Service ranger districts, the school agency) and the specialty work large primes subcontract: HVAC maintenance and grounds.
